home.title: Reeve: Discord moderation that records every action
home.description: A Discord moderation bot for one community. Every action becomes a numbered case, members are told why, and AI can only take small actions a person can undo.

hero.title: A Discord moderation bot that records every action and tells members why.

cases.title: Cases
cases.desc: Every action becomes one numbered record.
points: Records the action, the rule, and who took it, person or automation
Shows the member what happened and what they can do next
Notes and appeals stay attached to the case
Case numbers are never reused

reports.title: Reports
reports.desc: Members report a message, a profile or voice chat, and are told the outcome.
points: Report a message, a profile or voice activity, from the message or with /report
The message and ten either side are saved, by default
Repeat reports of the same message join one card
The reporter is told: action taken, already handled, or no action needed

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.desc: A private thread with the right staff.
points: Members choose a category and answer a short form
Only the opener and that category's staff are added
Staff claim, move and close tickets with buttons
A transcript is kept when it closes

appeals.title: Appeals
appeals.desc: Appeal once, and someone else reviews it.
points: Warnings, timeouts and bans can be appealed; a ban again after 30 days
Before a ban, the member is sent the appeal button first
Someone senior who wasn't involved in the case reviews it
Automated actions can be appealed straight away

ai.title: AI moderation
ai.desc: AI screens and summarises, and can only take small actions on its own.
points: Members' messages are screened first by a model on our own hardware
Flagged messages with a little context, and reports, go to a hosted model with names and IDs replaced
On its own it can delete a message or time out for up to an hour, and a person can undo both
Kicks, bans and role changes are always a person's call

rules.title: Rules
rules.desc: Every action cites a numbered rule.
points: Public and internal rules share the same numbers
Members see the rule number in every notice
Staff choose the rule when they act; AI can suggest one
Publish your rules to a channel with one command

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.desc: Kept only as long as needed, then deleted.
points: Message log: 14 days by default, or 7 to 30 if you choose
Saved report messages: one year after the report is resolved
Audit trail: six years, IDs and times only
AI only acts on rules you turn it on for

concerns.title: Concerns
concerns.desc: Ask admins to check how it was handled.
points: Offered when an appeal is turned down, a report closes with no action, or a member is kicked
Goes only to admins who weren't involved
Admins record a finding: no issue, guidance given, or decision changed
A monthly digest shows where guidance needs work

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.description: How Reeve turns every moderation action into a numbered case, tells members what happened, and lets them report, appeal and raise concerns.
howItWorks.heading: How Reeve handles moderation
howItWorks.lead: Every action becomes a numbered case. Members can report, appeal and raise concerns, and Reeve messages them with the outcome.

report.title: Report
report.desc: A member reports a message, a profile or someone's behaviour in a voice channel.
points: Report from the message, a profile, or with /report voice
The message and, by default, the ten either side are copied at once
Repeat reports about the same thing, made close together, join one card for your team
Every form asks which public rule applies, and Not sure is always an option

case.title: Case
case.desc: Every action becomes one numbered record.
points: Records the action, the rule, and who took it: a person, AutoMod or Reeve's automated review
Actions taken directly in Discord are recorded too, and staff add the rule
Appeals and staff notes stay with the case
Case numbers are never reused

notice.title: Notice
notice.desc: The member is told what happened, which rule, and what they can do next.
points: A heading that says what happened, in words
The public rule it cites, by number
When it ends, if it ends
Before a kick or a ban, the notice is sent first

appeal.title: Appeal
points: Warnings, timeouts, restrictions and bans can be appealed
Kicks can't, but the member can say a kick was a mistake
Nobody involved in the case decides the appeal
Automated actions can be appealed straight away

concern.title: Concern
concern.desc: Ask admins to check how something was handled.
points: Offered when an appeal is turned down, a report closes with no action, or after a kick
Goes to the staff who review concerns, admins by default
They record a finding: no issue, guidance given to the team, or decision changed

digest.title: Monthly digest
digest.desc: Shows admins where rules and guidance may need work.
points: Appeals made and overturned, and concerns with their findings
Rules, AutoMod rules and AI rules where appeals keep being overturned
It points to what may need revising, and people decide what to change

ai.title: AI moderation
ai.description: How Reeve uses AI: a local model screens chat, a hosted model reviews only what it flags and reports, with names replaced first, and AI can only delete a message or time a member out for up to an hour.
ai.heading: How Reeve uses AI
ai.lead: A model on our own servers screens members' messages. Only what it flags, and reports, go to a larger hosted model, with names replaced first. AI can take two small actions on its own, and only under rules your admins choose. Everything else is a person's decision, and a person can overrule every AI action.

stages.heading: The three stages
stages.intro: AI is off until an admin switches it on. When it is on, it works in three stages.

screen.title: Local screen
text: An open-weight safety model on our own servers reads members' messages in small batches: by default, every 10 messages or 30 seconds, in each channel.
If a batch looks fine, the result is discarded. We keep only daily counts, with nothing about who said what. No message leaves our servers at this stage.

review.title: Hosted review
text: When the screen flags messages, or a member reports something, a larger model from Anthropic (Claude), outside the UK, reviews them, with up to 10 earlier messages for context. It can ask once for more: by default, up to 50 earlier messages.

Names, user IDs, mentions, links, emails and phone numbers are replaced first. A name typed in plain text for someone Reeve hasn't seen before can get through, and the words themselves are still sent. Attachments are never sent; the model only sees that there was an image or a file.

example.label: An example of the names being hidden
lines: you clearly didn't read it, as usual

act.title: Act, or ask a person
text: For rules your admins have chosen, if the hosted review is sure enough to pass that rule's threshold, Reeve may act on its own, in one of two small ways. It never acts on staff, and by default not on anyone who joined a year ago or longer, or whose join date isn't known.
Anything else goes to a moderator as a suggestion, with the rule filled in for them to confirm or change.

limits.heading: What AI may do on its own

may.title: What AI may do
points: Delete a message
Time the member out for up to one hour, as well as deleting the message

never.title: What AI never does on its own
points: Warnings
Timeouts longer than one hour
Kicks and bans
Role changes
Anything flagged as safeguarding, which goes only to admins trusted with it

recorded.title: Every AI action is a case
recorded.text: Marked as Reeve's automated review, with an override card for your moderators.

control.title: Your rules, your thresholds
control.text: Choose which rules AI may act on and how sure it must be, or switch AI actions off at any time.

members.title: Members are told
members.text: The notice says automated moderation was involved. The member can say it was a mistake or appeal, and appeals against AI actions are marked as a priority and chased sooner.

card.title: A moderator can overrule every AI action in one click
points: Uphold action keeps it and marks it reviewed
Reverse action lifts the timeout and tells the member, if they accept messages, sending them the words that were deleted, as a deleted message can't be put back
Change sanction opens the form so a moderator can choose another
card.note: Try the buttons on the card. Decisions are counted rule by rule. By default, once a rule has 10 decided actions in 30 days, if more than one in five were reversed or changed, it goes back to suggesting only until an admin switches it back.

uphold: by {'@'}alex. The action stands, marked as reviewed.
reverse: by {'@'}alex. The timeout is lifted, and the member is told it was withdrawn and sent their words, if they accept messages.
change: Change sanction opens the moderation form. The new sanction replaces this one.

headings.open: Acted: message deleted, timed out for an hour. Waiting for review

never.heading: What AI never sees or does
points: Ordinary chat never goes to Anthropic. Only flagged messages with the messages just before them, reports, and summaries of reports and appeals that a moderator asks for do.

Staff messages, ticket threads and channels left out of logging are never screened. A staff message can appear, labelled as staff, as context beside a flagged message. Reports about staff are never sent to a hosted model.

Safeguarding concerns, and messages under rules your admins keep from AI, are never sent on or acted on by AI. They go only to admins trusted with safeguarding, and the card shows no content. A member's report is different: the hosted model reviews it, with names replaced, even if it touches on safeguarding or falls under a rule kept from AI, unless it is about staff.
If the local model is down, screening pauses and Discord's AutoMod carries on. Reeve never falls back to sending all chat to a hosted model.
Attachments never go to a hosted model. It sees only that a message had an image or a file.
For each hosted review, Reeve keeps a fingerprint of the prompt, by default for 12 months, never the prompt itself.

before.title: Suggestions first
before.text: AI actions stay off until an admin switches them on for a rule. Until then Reeve only suggests, so you can see how it does on your server first.

after.title: Reversals are tracked
after.text: We count how often moderators reverse or change AI actions, rule by rule. A rule reversed too often goes back to suggesting only.

monthly.title: A digest for admins
monthly.text: Each month, admins see which rules, AutoMod rules and AI rules had two or more decisions overturned on appeal, so they know where to look.

limits.text: AI makes mistakes, including mistakes that fall harder on some groups than others. Reeve keeps those mistakes small, visible and reversible; it cannot promise that every assessment is fair. Fairness depends on the people moderating, and Reeve gives them records and checks so they can show their working.
